summary: Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia and a PhD from Indiana University, and was attested as an assistant professor of religious studies at the University of Oklahoma in 2019.

Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, Peter J. Wilson, and Edmund Leach, later holding professorships at the University of Newcastle, Lancaster University, and Cardiff University.

Georg Buddruss (1929–2021) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1950–1954) and the University of Tübingen (~1954–1956), and served as a professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from circa 1963 to 1997.

Georg Bühler (1837–1898) specialized in Indology and linguistics. After earning his doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe and Theodor Benfey, he held posts at Elphinstone College, Deccan College, the University of Mumbai, and the University of Vienna.

Georg Curtius (1820–1885) was a linguist who studied at the University of Bonn and Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Christian Lassen, and Franz Bopp. He held posts at Charles University, the University of Kiel, and Leipzig University (~1862–1885).

Georg Morgenstierne (1892–1978) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1909–1914) and under Sten Konow (~1914–1921), and held a post at the University of Gothenburg (~1930–1937).

Georg Wilhelm Freytag (1788–1861) was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held positions at the University of Göttingen (~1811–1815) and served as a professor at the University of Bonn (~1819–1861).

Georg von Simson (born 1933) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as an editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1968 and served as a professor at the University of Oslo from circa 1977 to 2000.

Georg von der Gabelentz (1840–1893) was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Jena and Leipzig University, later holding professorships at Leipzig University (from 1878) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1889–1893).

George A. Keyworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and completed his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., later holding faculty posts at the University of Colorado Boulder and the University of Saskatchewan.

George Abraham Grierson (1851–1941) was a linguist and Indologist. He was educated at St. Bees School (~1864–1868) and Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1871), and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1873 to 1903.

George Baumann (born 1936) is an Indologist who earned his PhD from Heidelberg University in 1973. He served as Head of the Oriental Department at the Tübingen University Library from 1976 to 2001 and was affiliated with the University of Tübingen.

George Cardona (1936–2024) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at New York University (~1953–1956) and Yale University (~1957–1960), and spent his career as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1960 to 2005.

George Chemparathy (1928–2011) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Paul Hacker and Erich Frauwallner, and held academic posts at Loyola College, Chennai (~1952–1954) and Utrecht University (~1974–1993).

George Cœdès (1886–1969) specialized in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1904 to 1911 and served as president of the Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi around 1934.

George D. Bond (born 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD at Northwestern University, where he served as a professor of religion from circa 1974 to 2012.

George Foot Moore (1851–1931) was a scholar of religious studies. After studying at Yale University (~1868–1872), he served as a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (~1883–1901) and at Harvard University (~1901–1928).

George L. Hart (born 1942) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying at Harvard University (~1963–1969), he held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1974) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1974–2013).

George Lakoff (born 1941) is a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He completed studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1958–1962) and Indiana University (~1962–1966), and served on the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley (~1972–2016).

George Melville Bolling (1871–1963) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Loyola University Maryland and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at Catholic University of America (1895–1913), Johns Hopkins (1913–1914), and Ohio State University (1914–1939).
